card.text: A spiral galaxy 17.6 million parsecs away, seen close to edge-on.

sources.quote: Messier 98, M98 or NGC 4192 is an intermediate spiral galaxy about 44.4 million light-years away in slightly northerly Coma Berenices, about 6° to the east of the bright star Denebola.

introduction.text: Its picture is the Sloan Digital Sky Survey's, with stars removed, standing flat and facing the Sun. Its bulge stands through it as a volume, from a published fit.

sources.label: Wikipedia, "Messier 98"
sources.quote: It was discovered by French astronomer Pierre Méchain on 1781, along with nearby M99 and M100, and was catalogued by compatriot Charles Messier 29 days later in his Catalogue des Nébuleuses & des amas d'Étoiles.

optical.title: M98 in visible light
optical.summary: Flat picture facing the Sun; the bulge of a published fit stands through it. Depth is modelled.
